title: The customer concentration mistake that nearly broke a brokerage
seoTitle: The customer concentration mistake that nearly broke a brokerage
searchIntent: Why is customer concentration risky for a freight brokerage?
excerpt: A lesson from the early family business about losing a major account and rebuilding with a broader customer base.
takeaway: Do not let one busy customer replace a diversified book and an active sales process. Measure the exposure and build enough operating capacity to keep developing other relationships.

sections.title: Why is customer concentration risky for a freight brokerage?
paragraphs: Luis tells a story from the early family business, which started from scratch and grew over the years. A major customer provided steady work and supported much of the business. Servicing that account also consumed the time that might have gone into building other relationships.
Then the customer was acquired and its operation closed. The freight disappeared for reasons outside the brokerage’s control. A good relationship and strong past volume did not prevent the loss.

sections.title: Look beyond how busy the account makes you
paragraphs: A large customer can make the office feel successful while leaving the business dependent on a single decision elsewhere. Review the account’s share of revenue, gross profit, receivables and the team’s time. Each tells you something different about exposure.
Ask what would happen if the volume stopped or payment slowed. Could you meet existing commitments while rebuilding? This is a planning exercise, not a prediction that a valuable customer will leave.

sections.title: Build smaller relationships while the large account is healthy
paragraphs: Luis describes rebuilding with a broader base of customers and encouraging agents to develop smaller accounts alongside larger ones. The exact mix should fit the business; the principle is to avoid relying on one source of work.

Smaller does not automatically mean easier or more profitable. Evaluate service requirements and payment behavior for each account. The benefit of a broader book comes from several sound relationships, not merely adding names to a customer report.

sections.title: Protect sales time before you need replacement freight
paragraphs: Give customer development an owner and a place in the schedule. If service consumes every available hour, identify the support or process change needed to preserve both the current account and the future pipeline.

The family’s experience gives this lesson its weight: replacing lost work takes time. Build the next relationships while you can choose carefully, rather than waiting until an unexpected closure forces the business into urgent sales mode.
